name: pdmp-02-jump-processes
title: Phase 2 — Jump Process Layer: Discrete-Time → Continuous-Time Stochastic
claim:
Per-promoter and per-protein Poisson tau-leap samplers land in `poisson` mode. The acceptance gate
`pdmp-trajectory-distribution-match` FAILED: the cell_mass Poisson Wasserstein-2 grows monotonically
9.73 → 15.35 → 49.46. The decisive finding is negative but legitimate: cell_mass is the WRONG
observable for jump-process variance — the consumption_matched homeostat washes per-tick variance out
by construction, so Phase-3 inference must anchor on count-level listeners, not mass. (The "150 fg"
headline is max |Δ cell_mass| = 150 fg between configs — a transient on a single trajectory pair
computed in scripts/trajectory_divergence.py on the cell_mass quantity; it is NOT measured at the
rnap_data listener, and it cuts against this study's own thesis that cell_mass is the wrong observable.)
question:
Can v2ecoli's discrete-time stochastic layer (Poisson gene-
expression draws scaled by timestep/doubling time, the teleonomic
division trigger, and the globally-acting resource reallocation
correction) be replaced by a coherent continuous-time jump
process that, coupled with the Phase 1 metabolism ODE, satisfies
the Markov property of a piecewise-deterministic Markov process?
hypothesis:
(a) Replacing scaled-Poisson gene-expression draws with continuous-
time jump processes governed by explicit propensity functions
derived from measured kinetic constants (initiation, elongation,
degradation rates) reproduces the v2ecoli baseline trajectory
distribution within tolerance. (b) Replacing the teleonomic
doubling-time division trigger with a first-passage threshold
crossing in cell volume or total protein mass reproduces the
observed division-time distribution. (c) Replacing the global
resource reallocation step with affinity-based competition jumps
conserves mass and yields a clean PDMP — deterministic ODE flow
between jumps with state-dependent kernels at jumps.
objective:
Implement transcription_jump, translation_jump, and
division_threshold as Process Bigraph processes; replace the
global resource correction with jump-based competition reactions;
couple all jump processes with the Phase 1 metabolism ODE under
an integrated PDMP runner in Vivarium; verify the Markov property
(deterministic between jumps, specified kernels at jumps);
compare trajectory distributions vs. the v2ecoli baseline across
the Phase 0 conditions.
description:
Phase 2 of the v2ecoli → PDMP roadmap. The current discrete-time
layer is the most numerically suspect part of v2ecoli:
parametrization of stochastic draws depends on the ratio of the
fixed timestep to the teleonomic "doubling time" parameter
(DUF Sec. 4.1.1), and the global reallocation step exists to
paper over mass conservation violations introduced by the
composition of independent processes (DUF Sec. 2.1).

A PDMP-class formulation has neither: events occur at random
times drawn from explicit propensity functions, division is a
first-passage time of a continuous observable, and competition
for shared resources is encoded as state-dependent jump kernels
rather than a corrective fix-up step. The mathematical contract
to verify is that, between any two jumps, the state evolves
deterministically according to the coupled ODE (Phase 1
metabolism + any continuous components of expression machinery),
and that jumps occur at times specified by ∫ λ(s) ds = E for
E ~ Exp(1).

# Numerical considerations
Stochastic integration. Naive Gillespie SSA is exact but slow at
the propensity scales of mRNA/protein dynamics in a single cell
(10²–10⁴ events / s). The implementation choice (exact SSA vs.
τ-leaping vs. hybrid Anderson modified-next-reaction) trades
variance against compute and is justified per-process: e.g.,
ribosome-elongation events use τ-leaping with τ chosen so the
leap-condition (Δλ/λ < 0.03) holds; rare promoter-firing events
use exact next-reaction. Each choice carries a documented weak-
order and strong-order convergence claim.

Exponential-clock validation. The fundamental test of correctness
for a stochastic-jump implementation is that the cumulative
hazard ∫ λ(s) ds at successive events is Exp(1)-distributed.
We run this Anderson-Darling test over ≥10⁴ inter-event
intervals per jump process (α = 0.05). A failed test is the
smoking gun for a propensity bug.

First-passage validation. Cell division is a first-passage time
for volume crossing a threshold under the ODE+jump combined
dynamics. Before deploying on the full WCM we validate the
first-passage implementation on an analytical test problem
(Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, exact Bessel-function FPT
distribution) — the empirical FPT distribution from our
integrator must match the analytical CDF to KS distance < 0.02
over N=10⁴ trajectories.

Distribution-match resolution. Comparing trajectory ensembles
vs. v2ecoli baseline uses W₂ on summary statistic distributions
(growth rate, mean per-gene mRNA, mean per-gene protein,
division-time CV). N=200 PDMP trajectories per condition gives
W₂ MCSE ≈ σ_W₂/√200 ≈ 0.07 σ_W₂ — fine enough to detect
systematic deviations of ≥0.2 σ in the underlying distributions.
Sample size revisited if MCSE > 10% of the inter-baseline effect
size.

PDMP integrator validity. The Markov property is a structural
claim; we test it by re-simulating individual segments with the
same (state, RNG seed) and confirming bit-identical determinism
between jumps. Failure = leaky abstraction.

# Emitter
XArrayEmitter records every jump event as a row in a separate
zarr group ('jumps') alongside the continuous trajectory group
('continuous'), so the discrete-event time series and the ODE
segments can both be queried with xarray. max_generations=8 in
workspace.yaml accommodates the multi-generation division-time
CV / mother-daughter inheritance distributions that we compare
to v2ecoli baseline.

expected_behavior.name: jump-process-from-kinetics
expected_behavior.en: Every jump process (transcription, translation, division, competition) has a propensity function derived from measured or curated kinetic constants — no scaling by simulation timestep, no teleonomic "rates" derived from doubling-time targets.

expect.note: Acceptance band set as this test is built out (design-stage readout).

expected_behavior.name: division-first-passage
expected_behavior.en: Division events occur as first-passage crossings of a threshold in cell volume or total protein mass; the teleonomic doubling-time check is removed from the model.

expect.note: Acceptance band set as this test is built out (design-stage readout).

expected_behavior.name: pdmp-trajectory-distribution-match
expected_behavior.en: Summary statistics over PDMP trajectory ensembles (growth rate distribution, mean mRNA/protein abundances per gene, division-time CV) match the v2ecoli baseline distributions within specified tolerance across all ≥3 Phase 0 conditions. (Gating criterion.)

expect.note: GATE FAILED on cell_mass — the Poisson cell_mass Wasserstein-2 grows monotonically 9.73 → 15.35 → 49.46 (does NOT converge within tolerance). Per the closeout this is the wrong observable (consumption_matched homeostat washes per-tick variance out of cell_mass), so the negative result is reframed as structural — but the gate itself is FAILED, not passed/accepted.

expected_behavior.name: markov-property-verified
expected_behavior.en: Between any two jump events, state evolves deterministically under the ODE; jump times follow ∫ λ(s) ds = E for E ~ Exp(1). Verified by re-simulating segments with the same RNG seed and checking bit-identical determinism.

expect.note: Acceptance band set as this test is built out (design-stage readout).

expected_behavior.name: uq-exponential-clock-anderson-darling
expected_behavior.en: Cumulative hazard ∫λ(s)ds at successive events for each jump process passes an Anderson-Darling Exp(1) test (α=0.05) over ≥10⁴ inter-event intervals. The smoking-gun correctness test for a stochastic-jump implementation.

expect.note: Acceptance band set as this test is built out (design-stage readout).

expected_behavior.name: uq-fpt-analytical-validation
expected_behavior.en: The first-passage implementation, applied to an OU process with analytically known FPT distribution, recovers the analytical CDF to KS distance < 0.02 over N=10⁴ trajectories before being deployed on the WCM division mechanism.

expect.note: Acceptance band set as this test is built out (design-stage readout).

expected_behavior.name: uq-tau-leap-validity
expected_behavior.en: For every τ-leaping jump process, the leap-condition (max Δλ/λ < 0.03) is monitored; fraction of timesteps where it is violated must be <0.1% across the run. Above threshold, τ is shrunk or the process is switched to exact SSA.

expect.note: Acceptance band set as this test is built out (design-stage readout).

expected_behavior.name: uq-trajectory-w2-mcse
expected_behavior.en: Trajectory-distribution comparison vs v2ecoli baseline uses W₂ on summary distributions over N≥200 PDMP trajectories per condition; the W₂ MCSE is reported and required <10% of the cross-condition effect size before any tolerance decision is made.

report.conclusion: Predicted — replacing scaled-Poisson stochastics with continuous-time jumps from measured kinetic constants (Anderson-Darling Exp(1) verified), plus a first-passage division trigger, will yield a PDMP whose trajectory ensembles match v2ecoli baseline summaries within W₂ tolerance.
report.main_insight: The PDMP contract is the smoking-gun test for stochastic correctness: between-jump deterministic ODE flow + Exp(1) cumulative-hazard distribution. An A-D test on ≥10⁴ inter-event intervals catches every propensity bug.
report.caveat: τ-leaping for high-rate processes trades unbiasedness for compute — the leap condition (max Δλ/λ < 0.03) is monitored at every step and processes get switched to exact SSA when violated >0.1% of the time. NOTE on provenance: the per-sprint σ/μ/W2 summary table (base_mu/base_sd/pdmp_mu/pdmp_sd/w2_cm, incl. the cell_mass W2 progression 9.73 → 15.35 → 49.46) is HAND-ENTERED in scripts/phase2_progress_report.py (marked "Hardcoded here" so the report survives source-HTML churn) — it is transcribed, not recomputed at render time. Report figures are limited to the artifacts committed in this checkout (initiation-mode comparisons, event-rate / per-TU distributions, trajectory-divergence, ensemble-validation); the multi-gen inheritance / Gillespie / waiting-time figure set regenerates from a re-run of the phase0-multigen and jump-process pilots.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition: Continuous-time jump propensities (transcription, translation, division, resource competition) pass the Anderson-Darling Exp(1) test (α=0.05, ≥10⁴ inter-event intervals each). OU first-passage analytical validation: KS distance < 0.02. Trajectory-distribution W₂ vs. v2ecoli baseline within tolerance across all Phase 0 conditions. Markov property bit-verified.

resolved_uncertainties: Continuous-time per-promoter / per-protein Poisson tau-leap samplers were implemented and land in `poisson` mode. The "150 fg" headline is max |Delta cell_mass| = 150 fg between configs — a transient on a single trajectory pair, computed in scripts/trajectory_divergence.py on the cell_mass quantity (NOT measured at the rnap_data listener, which is a narrative literal absent from the computing script); and it cuts against this study's own thesis that cell_mass is the wrong observable.

cell_mass is decisively the WRONG observable for jump-process variance: the consumption_matched homeostat (from Phase 1) washes per-tick variance out of cell_mass by construction. Three controller- tuning attempts (tau-EMA, open-loop, sparse injection) all failed to recover mass variance.
remaining_uncertainties: The original Phase-2 gate `pdmp-trajectory-distribution-match` — trajectory-distribution W2 match to the v2ecoli baseline on cell_mass across all Phase-0 conditions — FAILED: the Poisson cell_mass W2 grows monotonically 9.73 → 15.35 → 49.46. Per the closeout this is the WRONG gate (cell_mass is the wrong observable), a legitimate negative/structural result — but the gate status is FAILED, not passed/accepted. A replacement count-level trajectory-distribution criterion has not yet been formally specified or passed.
The Anderson-Darling Exp(1) exponential-clock verification (>=1e4 inter-event intervals) and the OU first-passage division-trigger validation (KS < 0.02) remain unrun.

alternate_hypotheses.statement: It is the consumption_matched homeostat specifically (not jump sampling per se) that erases per-tick variance; loosening or disabling the homeostat would restore cell_mass as a usable variance observable.
alternate_hypotheses.why_plausible: The homeostat actively tracks a reference growth trajectory, so any per-tick fluctuation it sees is corrected within a tick.
discriminating_observables: cell_mass CV with the homeostat on vs off under identical jump seeds
count-listener variance (rnap_data, ribosome_data) vs cell_mass variance
evidence_for: Open-loop (homeostat-off) was one of the three tuning attempts.
evidence_against: Even open-loop, cell_mass did not become the right inference channel — pointing to counts, not mass, as the signal carrier.

mechanism_update_proposals.rationale: Anchor all downstream variance-based inference on count-level listeners (rnap_data, ribosome_data, monomer_counts) rather than cell_mass; the homeostat makes mass variance-blind. This redirected Phase 3.

followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Define and run a trajectory-distribution W2/KS criterion on count-level listeners (transcript/protein initiation counts) vs the v2ecoli baseline, replacing the cell_mass gate the closeout invalidated.

followup_study_proposals.title: Anderson-Darling Exp(1) exponential-clock + OU first-passage division validation
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Verify the cumulative hazard integral of lambda is Exp(1)-distributed over >=1e4 inter-event intervals (A-D, alpha=0.05) and validate the first-passage division trigger against an OU analytical CDF (KS < 0.02).

findings.statement: The Phase-2 trajectory-distribution-match gate FAILED on cell_mass: the Poisson tau-leap Wasserstein-2 grows monotonically rather than converging. The decisive (negative) finding is that cell_mass is the WRONG observable for jump-process variance -- the consumption_matched homeostat washes per-tick variance out by construction -- redirecting Phase-3 inference onto count-level listeners.

evidence.observed: cell_mass Poisson W2 grows 9.73 -> 15.35 -> 49.46 (monotonic; gate NOT met)

findings.next_action: Re-anchor the distribution-match test on count-level listeners (rnap_data / ribosome_data / monomer_counts).

findings.statement: Empirical confirmation of the Phase-2 redirect: across 4 seeds at 250 steps, every AGGREGATE observable (cell_mass, dry_mass, total monomer, ATP[c] count) washes out to ~0.028% cross-seed CV, while the DIRECT jump-event count (cumulative transcription-initiation events, rnap_data.rna_init_event) shows 0.85% CV -- ~30x higher. So the jump-process stochasticity is real but lives at the per-event count level, not in aggregate mass/pool observables the consumption_matched homeostat regulates -- which is exactly why Phase-3 inference must anchor on count-level listeners.

evidence.observed: CV: cell_mass 0.0285%, dry_mass 0.0288%, monomer 0.0273%, ATP 0.0283%, cumulative rna_init 0.846% (~30x)

findings.next_action: Build the count-level distribution-match gate (rna_init / monomer counts) as the Phase-2/3 acceptance criterion.
